subject: Urgent: ACME throughput regressions — suspected KV cache evictions
messages:
From: Claire D'Amato <claire@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Throughput drop / error spikes in 3/8 evening

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We started seeing significant throughput drops and a spike in 5xx errors on our production inference route (acme-main-chat) around 2026-03-08 20:40 UTC. Latency climbed from our 95th of ~180ms to sustained 600-900ms and QPS fell by ~35%. Ops oncall also saw a sharp increase in token-generation errors.

Sample symptoms:
- Multiple concurrent requests show long tails with stalled token streams (some > 4s per token)
- Error rate elevated to 2.7% from usual ~0.2%
- Host-level GPU utilization is normal; CPU spikes on host-side proxy 

We collected logs and attached a small bundle (redwood-logs-acme-20260308.zip). Can you confirm if anything changed on the Redwood side (batching or cache config) or if this looks like our workload hitting a configuration edge? This is impacting a customer-facing release; we need a prioritized path to mitigation.

Thanks,
Claire
Director of Product, ACME Corp

Subject: RE: Throughput drop / error spikes in 3/8 evening

Quick findings from the traces and profiler (attached kv-eviction-profiler.png):
- Observed frequent KV-cache evictions on the serving pool for acme-main-chat during 20:30–21:10 UTC. Eviction rate jumped ~9x compared to baseline.
- When eviction events occur, downstream worker threads stall waiting on KV refill; this looks like HOL (head‑of‑line) blocking where one large request prevents efficient batching for others.
- Batching windows remained aggressive (batch timeout 12ms) which, combined with high variance in request length, increases the chance that a long request will occupy the batch and force eviction churn.
- No recent kernel/runtime deploy in that window; config drift hypothesis: several tenants recently increased KV cache anti-affinity leading to reduced effective cache per-model.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low-risk, can be rolled within minutes):
1) Reduce batch timeout from 12ms -> 6ms for acme-main-chat to reduce long-request HOL exposure.
2) Increase KV cache cap for the pool by 25% (temporary bump) to reduce eviction rate.
3) Enable aggressive prefix/KV reuse for requests with stable prompt headers (ACME uses a shared system prompt).

I'll prepare a targeted rollout (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor eviction and 95p latency. Attaching profiler and single-run traces.

Rohan
Lead SRE, Serving Runtime

Claire — thanks for the fast repro bundle. We're executing Rohan's mitigations now:
- Rolling batch timeout change to 10% of traffic (canary) immediately, will expand based on eviction delta.
- Bumped KV cache cap on the serving pool by 25% (temporary).
- Enabled prefix reuse heuristics for the route.

Early indicators (15 minutes into canary):
- Eviction rate down ~60% in the canary population
- 95p latency for canary back to ~210–260ms
- Error rate in canary has dropped to 0.4%

We'll continue to expand canary if stable. If you prefer, we can schedule a brief post-mortem and permanent config change. Thanks for patience — will keep you updated.

Evelyn

- Root cause (current): KV cache saturation + HOL blocking exacerbated by aggressive batching window + increased per-tenant anti-affinity reducing effective cache.
- Mitigation applied: reduced batch timeout (canary -> rollouts), temporary KV cache cap bump, prefix reuse enabled. Canary results show fast improvement (95p latency back near baseline, error rate down to 0.4%).
- Next steps:
  - Rohan: prepare a follow-up change to make batch-timeout adaptive by request-length variance and add eviction-triggered autoscaling for KV cache.
  - Evelyn: schedule a post-mortem with ACME and share timeline to permanent configuration changes + SLA credits if requested.
  - Sean: work with ACME on a final verification window for their release.

I'll also loop in VP Eng/Prod operations for visibility; if ACME asks for credits or an SLA exception, I'll coordinate with Finance.
